name: Mapwhizz
headline: From a stalled launch
to a live product.
summary: A UK location-intelligence company was trapped in an over-budget, undelivered build. An honest audit, a stabilised core and a rebuilt frontend got the product into the market.
scope: Technical audit, backend stabilisation & frontend replacement

image.alt: Mapwhizz travel time analysis report detail, showing recommended office and commute comparisons.

challenge.title: Rescuing a stalled launch.
paragraphs: Mapwhizz had a strong proposition, but its chosen development partner could not deliver. The project was several times over the original budget, communication had broken down, and both halves of the software were buried in technical debt before the product had launched.
Walking away was not an option. The team needed someone to tell them the truth and find a way to market.

timeline.title: An honest audit
timeline.description: We assessed what could be saved and identified what needed replacing to reach launch.

timeline.title: Stabilisation and launch
timeline.description: A steadier core and a new frontend got the product into live use.

timeline.title: Rebuilding for scale
timeline.description: With the product serving customers, work began on the remaining legacy backend.

approach.title: Diagnosis: an honest audit.
paragraphs: We audited both halves of the application to see what could be saved. Instead of the ground-up rewrite that would have killed the budget and delayed launch indefinitely, we gave a straight recommendation: repair the critical core just enough to ship, and replace the broken part entirely.

approach.title: Stabilisation: getting the product over the line.
paragraphs: We separated and steadied the core logic, cut through the worst of the debt, and built the whole user-facing half from scratch. That got around the previous supplier’s bottlenecks and pushed the product into live use.

image.alt: Mapwhizz company dashboard with office details, available reports and credits, on a mint background.

approach.title: Scale, when the business was ready.
paragraphs: With the product live, stable and serving customers, Mapwhizz avoided a huge upfront rebuild. With revenue coming in, we moved on to the planned next phase: rebuilding what remained of the legacy system.

outcome.summary: The product is now live, stable, and serving users.
outcome.next: With the product in live use, work moved on to the planned rebuild of the remaining legacy backend for long-term scale.
paragraphs: Rebuilding the user-facing half first and phasing the rest into a later stage saved the launch, protected the budget, and set the business up to grow.
